still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month. It is printed on the branded box, and almost nobody pays it.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there.

The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot has not been revived, and Congress has not reopened the ~$41B CBO-scored permanent benefit. Medicare still pays for no weight-loss-only use and reaches users only through diagnosis codes (now including the widened dementia-risk and alcohol-use-disorder labels).

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands, and Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban in force.
The suicidal-ideation warning is still off the labels. Liraglutide is still the only incretin approved for children aged 6–11, and the two EEOC ADA charges over metabolic tracks are still pending.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Arithmetic: 31.0 ever-used − 21.5 current = 9.5 points of adults who used and are off now. 47% of ever-users have cycled = 14.6 points: ~12.4 are current users on at least a second course (~58% of current users, up from 53% because $49 generics make restarting cheap) and ~2.2 cycled and are off again. That leaves ~7.3 who stopped once and never restarted. This is consistent with one-year persistence near one-third and restart rates of 36–47%, now nudged up by price. Age check: 0.20×12 + 0.33×20 + 0.24×30.5 + 0.23×22.5 = 2.40 + 6.60 + 7.32 + 5.18 ≈ 21.5. Users: 21.5% of ~270M adults ≈ 58M. FICTIONAL payer mix: Medicare ~16.5M (28%), of whom ~13.2M are 65+, ~1.8M are under-65 disability/ESRD, and ~4.4M hold a dementia-risk code (up from 1.6M). Medicaid ~5.5M (9.5%), incl. ~0.9M on the AUD label since Apr 2032. Public total ~22M (38%), the single largest payer, up from 28% in 2030. Commercial ~13.7M (24%). Legitimate cash ~18.5M (32%): ~9M on generic semaglutide, ~7M on TrumpRx orals incl. amycretin, ~2.5M on direct branded injectables. Imported/counterfeit ~3.8M (6.5%), down from 5.2M. 65+ check: 22.5% × ~62M ≈ 14.0M = 13.2M Medicare + ~0.8M cash/commercial. The income gap narrowed (top-to-bottom 25 vs 17.5, from 23 vs 12) because generic price and the Medicaid AUD route reached the bottom third. The remaining gap is about clinicians, pharmacies and regain, not price. Off-drug population: ~25.6M adults used and are off now. Adult obesity is ~32.8%, and ~19% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug, concentrated in rural bottom-third counties and among adults under 30. Households with at least one current user: ~38%. Pediatric: ~1.6% of under-18s are on a drug: ~3.4% of 12–17s (generic semaglutide is driving growth) and ~0.4% of 6–11s on daily liraglutide, with off-label generic semaglutide under 12 now measurable.

access.public_coverage: Medicare is now the default payer for older users, with no new law behind it. Coverage follows the labels. Part D must cover a medically accepted indication, and the Jul 2031 tirzepatide extension (dementia risk, adults 60+ with obesity, no CVD required) made most obese beneficiaries eligible behind prior authorisation. FICTIONAL Part D arithmetic: dementia route 4.4M × ~$250 net × 12 ≈ $13.2B. The other ~12.1M users (diabetes, CV, CKD, OSA, AUD), ~58% of them on generic semaglutide at ~$40 net and the rest on brands at ~$230 net, average ~$120 × 12.1M × 12 ≈ $17.4B. Gross incretin spend is therefore ≈ $30.6B, against $29.7B in 2030: users rose ~67% while spend rose ~3% because of generics. Medicaid: the same 9 states still cover weight-loss use. Since Apr 2032 every state must cover oral semaglutide for alcohol use disorder, because AUD is not an excludable category under the rebate statute. ~5.5M users × ~$95 net × 12 ≈ $6.3B. EPSDT still pulls some children's drugs into Medicaid case by case.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide still sells for $5–35 a month abroad, but US-bound volume now pays 25% tariffs. Chinese export licensing on protected amino-acid intermediates squeezed Indian API makers for a quarter in late 2031. Brazil and Canada have multi-source generics (CAD 40–80). Chinese tirzepatide analogues sell across Southeast Asia and the Gulf.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Generic collapse: semaglutide's US compound patent expired in Dec 2031. Viatris, Hikma (made in Columbus, OH), Sandoz and Teva launched under settlement terms in Jan 2032, and Novo launched an authorised generic. By mid-2032 generic weekly semaglutide costs $45–69 a month cash (Cost Plus-type pharmacies at the low end), which is ~10× India's price, down from ~40×. Branded products did not follow all the way down: Zepbound/Wegovy direct $249–329, Foundayo $149–249, oral amycretin $299 (list $1,199), MariTide $279. Employer coverage rose 36% → 40% only because generic-only weight benefits cost under ~$600 a year per member. Brands sit behind step therapy. Metabolic tracks shrank from ~4.5M to ~3.9M (inside the 13.7M commercial users), and some insured workers pay $49 cash to stay out of adherence verification. Orals are ~46% of users. The cheapest product is a needle and the best pill is ~6× its price. Access is now an income-floor question: a clinician visit, a pharmacy, a refrigerator, $49 spare, and staying on long enough to beat regain. The gray market is now mostly 'research-grade' retatrutide and amycretin peptides and residual Indian vials. Tariffs and legal $49 generics squeezed it.

GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1 agonist/GIP-receptor antagonist antibody conjugate, monthly injectable (MariTide)
GLP-1/amylin co-agonist, daily oral (amycretin oral, approved Aug 2031)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)

drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Oral parity is realised by amycretin. The Oct 2029 filing was the daily oral formulation. After an extended review it was approved Aug 2031, with ~20% weight loss at 72 weeks and non-inferiority to tirzepatide 15 mg in a head-to-head trial. Its phase 3 used SHAPS anhedonia scoring at FDA request. Subcutaneous amycretin remains in phase 3 with no filing. The AUD indication followed the rules: phase 3 readout Feb 2031, sNDA filed Mar 2031, approval Apr 2032, 13 months later. Tirzepatide's dementia extension was under review at the start and was approved Jul 2031. Generic semaglutide entered after compound-patent expiry and settlements (see events), so generic_us is true for semaglutide only. Tirzepatide has no US generic. The 'mood and motivation' driver is realised through marketing, not approval: no incretin carries a mood indication, but telehealth services sell low-dose generic semaglutide as 'quiet mind' plans, and no agency has acted. Implant programmes remain preclinical/phase 1. Bimagrumab-type muscle adjuncts read out phase 3 in 2032 but have not been filed. Global incretin market ~$150B (2031). US net prices fell sharply on semaglutide and drifted on brands.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Oral amycretin's GI rates are similar to tirzepatide's. Chronic diarrhoea in long-term users is now routinely screened for exocrine insufficiency.
Elevated with rapid weight loss; unchanged.
No causal confirmation of acute pancreatitis; absolute risk low. Litigation now pleads exocrine insufficiency alongside it.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; post-2029 filings consolidating in a new MDL.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The hip-fracture HR holds at ~1.3 in users 65+ after >2 years and ~1.45 in people who have cycled 3+ times. The dementia-route population nearly tripled to ~4.4M, which raised absolute fracture counts in Medicare. Early registry data on oral amycretin show lean-mass loss similar to tirzepatide's.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning retained. Many Part D plans now require a baseline DXA for dementia-route prior authorisation, a plan practice rather than a federal rule.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed in adverse reactions; no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new signal, including in the SHAPS-instrumented amycretin trials.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The first randomised data came from SHAPS-scored amycretin and retatrutide phase 3s: clinically meaningful anhedonia in 6.8% on drug vs 2.9% on placebo, dose-related, ~10–11% at top retatrutide and amycretin doses. These match the 2029 observational cohort's ~7–8% vs ~3%. Across ~58M users, the ~4-point excess implies roughly 2.3–2.6M attributable cases. Most resolve within 6–10 weeks of dose reduction or stopping.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Oct 2031 class labelling under Warnings and Precautions ('Anhedonia and emotional blunting'), with the prevalence figure and dose-reduction advice. Medication Guides updated. No boxed warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months, worse after repeated cycles. Cheap generics shortened gaps between courses, but more users now take short holidays for blunting and regain partially between them.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; it underpins chronic-therapy framing and adherence monitoring.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: B12, iron and vitamin D deficiency in low-intake users. Fat-soluble vitamin deficiency is linked to exocrine insufficiency. Elevated among older dementia-route users with low intake.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Label language added 2031 recommending periodic micronutrient assessment in long-term users.

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: A third cohort (Israeli Clalit, 2031) replicated the Danish and Optum findings for semaglutide at ~4 per 1,000 person-years after 5+ years vs ~2 in controls. Partial recovery of faecal elastase within 12 months of stopping was seen in about half of cases. Tirzepatide shows a smaller, non-significant excess in thinner 5-year data. The generic launch puts millions on indefinite low-cost semaglutide.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Semaglutide labels (brand and generic) carry a W&P with faecal elastase testing guidance (Mar 2031). Class labelling for other agents is pending. EMA PRAC added it to semaglutide SmPCs.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in adolescents and children on drug for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About ten years of semaglutide follow-up now exist. The first pediatric bone-density interim report (liraglutide 6–11, 2-year) shows slightly slower BMD accrual of uncertain clinical meaning. Lifetime-exposure questions sharpen as cheap generics reach adolescents.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric postmarketing requirements continue; the FDA asked for 5-year growth data before considering any under-12 semaglutide filing.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Poison-centre calls fell from ~4× to ~3× 2025 levels as legal $49 generics displaced counterfeit pens. Harms now concentrate in 'research-grade' retatrutide and amycretin peptides sold by social shops.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Import alert and pen serialisation retained. Tariffs did more than enforcement to reduce mail volume. Personal-importation enforcement is still weak.

safety_ledger.effect: Quality and immunogenicity variation in synthetic generic semaglutide
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Case series of anti-drug antibodies and reduced response, reported after API sourcing shifted under tariffs and Chinese export licensing. Absolute rates are low, and no batch-level pattern has been confirmed.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA impurity-profile requirements for synthetic peptide ANDAs apply. Surveillance is through FAERS; no action yet.

food_and_beverage.state: About 38% of households now have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~10–12% from 2025 and sugary drinks ~9%. Generic price compression spread use into lower-income zip codes, which weakened the value-pack refuge. Private-label snack volumes fell for the first time. Protein and fibre lines are mainstream rather than premium, and whey prices eased as capacity caught up. Senior-community food service (Florida, Arizona) is cutting portion sizes as the dementia route spreads.

alcohol.state: US spirits volumes are down ~14% from 2025 and beer ~9%. The AUD approval and ASAM guideline moved alcohol reduction from EAP off-label use to a covered Medicaid and Part D indication. Heavy-drinker volume is the most exposed. Distributors in Ohio, Indiana and Michigan consolidated further. Non-alcoholic lines grow but are small.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat to slightly down. Checks are smaller. Casual-dining chains that leaned on alcohol attach are closing locations in mid-sized Midwestern cities. QSR value menus hold but no longer grow as lower-income use rises. 'Half plate' pricing is common.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep shrinking. Mass retailers now stock narrower size curves, while stretch, resale and rental serve holiday-takers and cyclers. A small backlash market sells 'Big Table'-branded clothing and fat-positive lines through social commerce.

fitness.state: Strength training and DXA scanning keep growing, helped by Part D plans asking for baseline scans. Senior strength programmes at YMCAs and Medicare Advantage gyms are the fastest-growing segment. Premium DXA-plus-coaching memberships hold at $250–400 a month.

insurance.state: Employer pharmacy trend fell to ~+4% in 2032 on generic semaglutide. Coverage rose modestly to 40% on generic-only designs. Adherence-differential programmes persist under the 2027 guidance but shrank with the metabolic tracks. Part D bids rose again on dementia-route volume, though less than feared because generics took most other volume.

pharma.state: Novo's US semaglutide revenue fell steeply after generic entry, partly cushioned by its authorised generic and oral amycretin. Lilly, holding tariff-free US API capacity, the dementia franchise and retatrutide, is the de facto national champion. Hikma, Viatris, Sandoz and Teva split a high-volume, low-margin generic market. Indian makers lost US mail volume to tariffs but grew elsewhere.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Thinness has stopped signalling money, because $49 buys it. Muscle and skin still do. The soft, slightly depleted thin body now reads as generic. The lean, lifted body reads as coached. A new figure is common in Florida's retirement corridor: the very thin grandparent on the dementia route, whose walking cane is read as a fracture precaution. In lower-income neighbourhoods regainers are still visible, but fewer, and more of them are taking holidays than have lost access.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Price dropped out of the class equation and was replaced by maintenance. In Charlotte and Austin, lean-mass percentage is still status. In the Columbus logistics corridor, workers increasingly buy Hikma's locally made generic at $49 rather than accept the plant clinic's monitored monthly shot. Among bottom-third women aged 50–64 in Ohio and Kentucky, generic semaglutide brought many regainers back on, now paying cash. Among under-30s, being unmedicated is becoming an identity in its own right, strongest in Bread Alone towns and art scenes.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals are short and protein-forward. The backlash made big meals political. 'Bread Alone' claims ~1,300 congregations across Oklahoma, Arkansas and Texas and now hosts Sunday 'full table' dinners after fasting weeks. Detroit's 'Big Table' potlucks, a fat-acceptance revival started by Black women organisers, draw thousands monthly. School lunch fights now include teenagers on generic semaglutide.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Apps kept the 'lean-mass verified' badges and added a 'holiday-friendly' tag, an informal signal that the user doses down for dates. Desire mismatch is a standard couples-therapy topic. Some MariTide couples have switched to weekly generics so they can control timing again.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite has become a public argument. Upper-tier culture still treats it as managed noise. The backlash now has a shared vocabulary: Unmuted's 'Full Volume' tour, Big Table, the fasting churches, and MAHA-adjacent influencers who added 'foreign peptides' and Lilly's champion status to their anti-pharma message. They disagree about almost everything except that hunger and pleasure are not symptoms. The Sept 2032 'Whole Appetite' rally in Tulsa drew ~25,000.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Now on the label: clinically meaningful anhedonia in ~6.8% of users vs ~2.9% on placebo, ~10–11% at top doses, roughly 2.3–2.6M attributable cases among ~58M users. Mild 'evenness' is reported by a much larger share and is the main reason given for dose reduction and holidays.
interior_life.framing: There are three framings at once. The label calls it 'anhedonia and emotional blunting'. Telehealth subscription plans sell low-dose generic semaglutide as 'quiet mind'. In ordinary speech it is 'the hush', and people say they are 'taking a loud week' when they skip a dose. HR largely dropped 'steadiness' from competency language after the Oct 2031 label, on counsel's advice.
interior_life.effect_on_work: About 3.9M workers remain in adherence-verified tracks under the unchanged 2027 guidance. Since the label, most large operators (Columbus logistics, national call centres, the Texas and Indiana state plans) added 'dose review' forms that let enrollees step down without losing the premium differential, provided they stay on. Supervisors now ask about 'loud weeks' the way they ask about migraines. The EEOC charges are still pending. Upper-tier firms monitor nothing.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Unmuted's off nights became the 'Full Volume' tour, booked into union halls in Detroit, Baltimore and Cleveland. Comedians do 'loud week' material. The 'flat' fiction imprint added a memoir line about coming back from the hush. Sportsbooks' wagering per account fell further. Bars in mid-sized cities keep closing as AUD treatment becomes covered.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Drug holidays are normal and cheap: weekly generic users skip a dose before anniversaries and trips. Therapists report fewer 'parallel lives' than in 2030 and more negotiated schedules. Some partners now ask each other, in so many words, whether they are on a loud week.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The backlash is visible but has no legislation to show for it. No state passed a premium ban, and Congress did nothing. In the 2032 campaigns incretins came up as a price victory claimed by both parties and as a 'foreign peptide' tariff issue, not as a mood issue. Neither national ticket proposed weight-loss coverage. The AUD-code route has drawn quiet concern from civil-liberties groups over what a diagnosis on a Medicaid record means for custody and licensing.

state.regulatory_posture: No new health legislation, coverage rules or premium rules at any level. FDA activity was routine: approvals (tirzepatide dementia extension, oral amycretin, oral semaglutide for AUD), ANDA approvals for semaglutide, and class labelling for anhedonia. No agency acted on 'quiet mind' telehealth marketing. Public coverage widened entirely through existing statute: labels moved, and Part D and Medicaid rebate rules followed automatically.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: None new. TrumpRx still operates on manufacturer-set prices. The Bridge pilot has not been revived. The 2027 tri-agency 30% wellness guidance stands.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Unchanged in law. Clinic administration records, PBM fills and app logs still flow to wellness vendors under consent forms, which now include the anhedonia label text. Two state Medicaid programmes still condition weight-loss coverage on adherence and BMI progress. AUD diagnoses created by the new Medicaid route now sit in claims records.
state.workforce_or_military: TRICARE rules are unchanged, and the Army recruit oral pilot continues without expansion. With an approved AUD indication, DOT's pending question about drivers on incretins for alcohol is sharper, but it has still not ruled.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: In May 2031 Section 232 tariffs put 25% on Indian and 50% on Chinese finished incretins and peptide APIs, exempting product made from US-synthesised API. Beijing responded with export licensing on protected amino-acid intermediates. India filed a WTO consultation. Lilly's Indiana, North Carolina and Texas plants made it the tariff-free national champion. Novo shelters behind its North Carolina fill-finish and the EU tariff cap. US generic prices settled ~10× India's rather than ~40×.

events.event: Commerce imposes Section 232 tariffs of 25% on Indian and 50% on Chinese incretin products and peptide APIs, exempting US-synthesised API. China answers with export licensing on peptide intermediates, and Lilly's US plants leave it the only major maker fully outside the tariff wall.

FDA extends tirzepatide's dementia-risk indication to adults 60+ with obesity without cardiovascular disease. Part D plans must cover it as a medically accepted indication, and by late 2032 about 4.4 million beneficiaries hold the code, making Medicare the largest single payer for incretins.

FDA approves Novo's daily oral amycretin, filed in October 2029, at ~20% weight loss and non-inferior to tirzepatide 15 mg head-to-head. It is the first pill to match the leading injectables, priced at a $1,199 list and $299 through TrumpRx.

FDA adds class labelling for 'anhedonia and emotional blunting' to all incretins, citing 6.8% vs 2.9% placebo in SHAPS-scored trials. Within weeks, telehealth services begin selling low-dose generic semaglutide as 'quiet mind' plans, and large employers strip 'steadiness' from competency frameworks.
events.driver: safety_signal: anhedonia_labelled; new_indications: mood_and_motivation; personality_layer: mainstream_complaint

events.event: Semaglutide's US compound patent expires and Viatris, Hikma, Sandoz and Teva launch generics under settlement terms, alongside a Novo authorised generic. By July, cash prices for weekly generic semaglutide run $45–69 a month.

FDA approves oral semaglutide for alcohol use disorder, 13 months after Novo filed on a February 2031 phase 3 readout that ASAM had already written into guidelines. Because AUD is not an excludable category, every state Medicaid programme must now cover it.

open_tensions: The Medicaid AUD route is now the cheapest legal door for poor adults in the 41 states that exclude weight loss. Clinicians are coding borderline drinkers to get patients covered, and those diagnoses sit permanently in claims records that custody courts, licensing boards and DOT may eventually read.

Medicare's dementia route nearly tripled in the oldest, most fracture-prone users, onto a drug class whose first decade-scale signal (exocrine insufficiency) is now labelled for semaglutide. The tirzepatide confirmatory dementia trial has not read out, and Part D bids keep rising.

The same reward modulation is labelled as an adverse effect and sold as 'quiet mind'. Adherence-conditioned premiums still stand under the 2027 guidance, so employees in metabolic tracks may dose down but not stop, and the EEOC charges remain undecided.

The $49 generic floor depends on US-synthesised API behind a tariff wall and Chinese intermediate licensing. One supply squeeze or a confirmed generic immunogenicity signal would push cash users back toward research-grade peptides.

prose.headline: The $49 Hush: semaglutide goes generic, Medicare becomes the payer, and the label finally admits what it does to joy
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2032 a little over one American adult in five takes an incretin drug, and nearly a third have tried one. The drug did not become more wonderful. It became cheap, then covered, and then honestly described, in that order.

The cheapness came on schedule. Semaglutide's American compound patent ran out in December 2031. In January four generic makers and Novo itself launched copies of the weekly shot, and by summer a month's supply cost between $45 and $69 at a cash pharmacy. One of the busiest generic lines is made in Columbus, Ohio. That location is not incidental. In May 2031 Washington put tariffs on Indian and Chinese peptide products and their raw materials, Beijing answered by licensing the chemical building blocks, and the only way to sell into America without the tariff was to make the active ingredient here. Lilly, which had built that capacity years earlier, became the national champion. The price gap with India fell from forty-fold to about ten-fold, and the counterfeit pens that killed people in 2029 lost most of their customers to a legal product that cost less.

The coverage came through the labels, without a vote. In July 2031 the FDA extended tirzepatide's dementia-risk claim to anyone over sixty with obesity, heart disease or not. Medicare still cannot pay for weight loss, but it must pay for that. More than four million older Americans now hold the code, and Medicare is the largest single payer for these drugs. In April 2032 an oral semaglutide was approved for alcohol use disorder. Because federal law does not let Medicaid exclude that category, every state program now covers it. In the forty-one states that never paid for weight loss, the alcohol diagnosis has become the door. Doctors in Kentucky clinics admit, carefully, that some of the drinking they document is modest.

The honesty came from randomised trials that had finally been asked the right question. Newer studies measured pleasure, and in October 2031 the FDA put it on every label: about seven users in a hundred lose a clinically meaningful share of pleasure, against three on placebo, more at high doses. Within weeks, telehealth firms were selling low-dose generic semaglutide as a 'quiet mind' plan, citing the same mechanism. No agency objected. Large employers, on their lawyers' advice, quietly deleted 'steadiness' from their competency frameworks but kept their monitored programs, and added a form for requesting a lower dose. People now talk about 'the hush' the way they talk about sleep. A week off the drug is called 'a loud week', and skipping a dose before an anniversary costs nothing when the shot is $49.

The needle stopped mattering in August 2031, when Novo's oral amycretin matched tirzepatide in a head-to-head trial. That pill costs $299 a month. The generic injection costs a sixth of that, so most people who want the pill pay extra to avoid a needle they no longer fear.

The bottom third gained most. Its usage rate rose by half, because price stopped being the barrier. What remains is a clinic, a pharmacy and the patience to stay on. A thin body no longer says much about money. Muscle still does. In Florida's retirement towns the newest visible type is the very thin grandparent with a fracture-precaution cane.

The backlash grew loud without winning anything. Fasting churches across Oklahoma and Texas, Detroit's Big Table potlucks, Unmuted's Full Volume tour and the anti-pharma influencers who now attack 'foreign peptides' and Lilly with equal heat filled a Tulsa fairground in September. No legislature acted on any of it. From a distance the country looks a little thinner and a little quieter, and it can now say why.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Marlene Hooks, sixty-seven, sets her coffee down on the new Medication Guide. It is folded into the Zepbound box beside the pen, and she reads the yellow-highlighted paragraph twice: about 7 in 100. She thinks of her Thursday canasta group and tries to count.

The pharmacy in Kettering charged her $62 for the month. The Part D plan wanted the bone scan first, so in March she lay on a cold table while a technician said 'hold still, hon.' Her hip was fine. Her mother's wasn't.

Roy is at the counter splitting a generic semaglutide pen he gets for forty-nine dollars, cash, because Medicare won't pay for his. 'Loud week for me,' he says. Their granddaughter turns nine on Saturday. He wants to taste the cake.

Marlene doesn't skip. She doesn't know what she would be skipping toward.

At eleven she drives her sister Darla to the church on Wilmington Pike. Darla has joined the fasting women from Bread Alone, who meet in the basement and talk about hunger as though it were a gift. Darla is heavier than she was in 2028 and seems happier. Marlene waits in the car with the radio on, listening to a man explain tariffs on Chinese amino acids.

In the afternoon she walks the Kroger loop twice with her cane. It is a precaution, not a need. She buys half a sheet cake.

That night Roy eats a second slice standing up and laughs at something on the television. Marlene watches him laugh. She has the clear, mild thought that it looks like a lot of work, and that she used to do it too.

least_plausible_claims.quote: making Medicare the largest single payer for incretins
least_plausible_claims.why: Fails magnitude/reconciliation: the candidate's own payer mix puts Medicare at ~16.5M (28%) and legitimate cash at ~18.5M (32%). Only the combined 'public total' of Medicare and Medicaid (38%) is largest, so the claim contradicts the user counts.

least_plausible_claims.quote: The first randomised data came from SHAPS-scored amycretin and retatrutide phase 3s
least_plausible_claims.why: Fails mechanism: retatrutide was approved Mar 2029 and amycretin was filed Oct 2029, both before the parent's 'no randomised data' state. The parent shows no SHAPS scoring in those programmes, so it is unclear when those phase 3s ran, and the result conveniently matches the 2029 observational 7–8% vs 3%.

least_plausible_claims.quote: incl. ~0.9M on the AUD label since Apr 2032
least_plausible_claims.why: Fails magnitude and mechanism: 0.9M Medicaid enrollees stabilised on a newly approved oral drug within about eight months of approval is very fast. It needs state formulary and prior-authorisation implementation and diagnosis coding at scale, and the candidate gives no ramp.

least_plausible_claims.quote: The first randomised data came from SHAPS-scored amycretin and retatrutide phase 3s
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: retatrutide was approved in Mar 2029, so its phase 3s predate any FDA request for SHAPS scoring, which the world ties to amycretin. Class labelling for every incretin also follows only about two months after amycretin's approval, which is a convenient shortcut.

The result is a harder but more legible society, so I score it a bit above a worse 2030.
